description: Real S2: genesis rescan on a wallet whose seed we own, with a populated UTXO pool. Recovered into a fresh console_wallet via --recovery against a fresh base-path.
wallet_seed_words: doctor exist smoke swing sibling okay endless unusual tent soda wire badge happy vague monster maximum cherry quiz crash friend crunch lumber unique vintage

setup.step_1: From mining wallet, gRPC Transfer with 100 PaymentRecipients all targeting Mode 2 wallet's address. 21 of 100 succeeded (mining wallet partially saturated).
setup.step_2: Wait for the 21 outbound txs to reach TX_MINED_UNCONFIRMED.
setup.step_3: Stop Mode 2 daemon (not necessary - recovery uses separate base-path).
setup.step_5: Wallet derives the same view+spend keys from the seed, scans from birthday block through tip, detects every output addressed to this address (the original 30k S0 tx + 21 new 100 tXTM fragments).

earlier_incidental_recovery_n1.note: earlier in session, less warm cache

caveats: Spec target was the 512-UTXO pool from S1. We have 22 UTXOs - intermediate but real. Push to 100+ requires waiting for more mining-wallet fragments to confirm, or running S1-style coin_split on the recovered wallet.
Most of the throughput is base-node-side block delivery - the 22 UTXO detections take negligible time relative to walking 674k empty blocks.

blocks_per_sec varies meaningfully with OS page cache state. The earlier incidental N=1 recovery hit 24,344 blocks/sec; this N=22 run hit 37,025. The per-UTXO storage cost is small enough that cache warmth dominates.
what_we_proved: console_wallet's --recovery + --seed-words path produces a real S2 measurement against a wallet with a real UTXO pool.
End-to-end reproducibility: anyone with the seed can spawn a fresh wallet and observe the same recovery.
Pure block-walk throughput (1.5M blocks/min on this host) is well above wallet-internal accounting overhead for tens of UTXOs.
fix_for_higher_utxo_count: Send more fragments through mining wallet (rate-limited by mining wallet saturation - need to wait for its prior coin_split outputs to confirm).
Or run S1 doubling/fanout against the recovered wallet (already has 32k tXTM available).
